### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/hono`, `@objectstack/plugin-hono-server`, `@objectstack/service-storage`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **48** documentable anchor(s).

**14** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/client-sdk.mdx`  _(via ERROR_CODE_LEDGER (symbol, a top-level const object))_
- `content/docs/api/error-catalog.mdx`  _(via ERROR_CODE_LEDGER (symbol, a top-level const object), PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE (literal, a string literal in ERROR_CODE_LEDGER; a string literal in PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE_CODE; a string literal in isTransportBodyTooLarge))_
- `content/docs/api/error-handling-server.mdx`  _(via ERROR_CODE_LEDGER (symbol, a top-level const object))_
- `content/docs/api/index.mdx`  _(via HonoHttpServer (symbol, a top-level class), createHonoApp (symbol, a top-level function))_
- `content/docs/api/wire-format.mdx`  _(via HonoHttpServer (symbol, a top-level class), createHonoApp (symbol, a top-level function))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/import-mappings.mdx`  _(via PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE (literal, a string literal in ERROR_CODE_LEDGER; a string literal in PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE_CODE; a string literal in isTransportBodyTooLarge))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/virtual-objects.mdx`  _(via statusCode (symbol, a field of class RequestBodyTooLarge))_
- `content/docs/frontend/data-objectstack.mdx`  _(via statusCode (symbol, a field of class RequestBodyTooLarge))_

- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via describeEffectiveAccess (sdk, the bare tail of client method security.describeEffectiveAccess, bound to GET /api/v1/security/users/:id/effective-access))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/error-handling.mdx`  _(via HonoHttpServer (symbol, a top-level class), createHonoApp (symbol, a top-level function), PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE (literal, a string literal in ERROR_CODE_LEDGER; a string literal in PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE_CODE; a string literal in isTransportBodyTooLarge))_

⛔ **7** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via ERROR_CODE_LEDGER (symbol, a top-level const object))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via ERROR_CODE_LEDGER (symbol, a top-level const object))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **9** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **176** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 88355328f0399bec54337791a6656b8b385d3644` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `1a37cc35bf5dda750c101dc07455e048617582b3` — the merge of head `bb70828123790b3d9fdc3f58bdc1f8bf19389c2b` into base `88355328f0399bec54337791a6656b8b385d3644`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 1a37cc35bf5dda750c101dc07455e048617582b3 && git checkout 1a37cc35bf5dda750c101dc07455e048617582b3
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 88355328f0399bec54337791a6656b8b385d3644 bb70828123790b3d9fdc3f58bdc1f8bf19389c2b && git checkout -B drift-repro 88355328f0399bec54337791a6656b8b385d3644 && git merge --no-ff bb70828123790b3d9fdc3f58bdc1f8bf19389c2b

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 88355328f0399bec54337791a6656b8b385d3644
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 88355328f0399bec54337791a6656b8b385d3644` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

security#2 · os-tesla · session_01L9qibwMmGJKaQ52CgHqNu2

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `e85a506291951440231cda9eef79277062b18d45`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/src/body-limit.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/src/request-body.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/src/adapter.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/src/hono-plugin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/src/index.ts, packages/adapters/hono/src/index.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/storage-routes.ts, scripts/check-route-envelope.mjs

The rest of the diff (the three test files and `.changeset/request-body-limit.md` as prose) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`. Read: claim 6866240706, amendments 6866365896 and 6867307355, dev report 6867865935, the PR body, the net diff against `5e250a65` (13 files), and the check-runs on this head.

Check-runs on this head, all completed: 56 success, 13 skipped, 0 failed, 0 pending. Among them `Check Changeset`, `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Spec property liveness`, `Type Check · workspace`, `Test Core` 1/8 to 8/8, `Dogfood Regression Gate` and both `PR-body guards` runs are success.

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept set, narrowed, right: on both doors a JSON, form or other body over the limit that was read before is answered `413 PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE`. The limit is 10 MiB by default. Exactly the limit is read as before (`count` over `limit`, and the hold loop reads on at `total` equal to `limit`).
- Accept set, unchanged, right: the three `rawBody()` byte doors in `storage-routes.ts` (chunk PUT, upload-link PUT, presigned raw PUT) are served the original body, so each is judged by `max_upload_mb` as on `main`. No other package in the tree calls `rawBody()`.
- Accept set, unchanged, right: the upload link's several-file form is judged by its own form limit (`max_upload_mb` times the files the link takes, plus 64 KiB), above the transport limit. A declared length over that limit is refused before the form is read. An undeclared form past that limit is read whole and then refused, which is the remainder the seat named for the next PR.
- Public surface, widened, right: `HonoPluginOptions.maxRequestBodyBytes`, `ObjectStackHonoOptions.maxRequestBodyBytes`, `HonoHttpServer.setMaxRequestBodyBytes()` and `getMaxRequestBodyBytes()`, `OS_HTTP_MAX_BODY_BYTES`, and nine `body-limit` exports from the package index. The PR body and changeset name all of them.
- Error-code vocabulary, unchanged, right: `PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE` is already registered by `@objectstack/rest`. The diff adds one provenance row and no code.
- `packages/spec` holds no other change, and no option key is added to it, as amendment 6866365896 states.

### ② Semver level

- `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` is the right line for this diff: the published surface changes, and a body both doors read today is now refused. The line is line-initial and identical in the PR body and the changeset. Amendments 6866365896 and 6867307355 still read `Clause-②: no`. The PR's line is the one that matches the tree, and the claim line is the seat's to amend.
- `Metadata-protocol: none` is right: nothing a metadata author writes changes. With `none`, the level is `patch` on each package the diff moves, and the changeset takes `patch` on `@objectstack/plugin-hono-server`, `@objectstack/hono` and `@objectstack/service-storage`.
- The breaking arm carries what it owes: `!` in the title, a `**BREAKING**` banner that says who moves and how (raise `maxRequestBodyBytes` or `OS_HTTP_MAX_BODY_BYTES`, or send the content through a storage upload door), and exactly one adr-0087 marker, `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, with its reason. `Check Changeset` is success on this head.
- Nit N1: the changeset frontmatter does not list `@objectstack/spec`, although the diff moves `packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts`. Earlier ledger-row changesets list it (#32932, #32926). All four packages sit in one `fixed` group, so the published versions are the same either way. Only the spec changelog misses the entry.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions` in the dev report is empty.
- Deviation, over-limit requests still reach the route: accepted by the seat. In the code, nothing is read past the limit, and the read answers 413.
- Deviation, the signature trailer is an HTML comment: no contract effect.
- Out-of-scope items in the dev report: counting an undeclared body against `max_upload_mb` through `rawBody({ maxBytes })`, the undeclared form counted against its own limit, and `max_upload_mb` unset. The first two are ordered for the next PR. The third is kept as it is. None is owed by this diff.
- The dev report names head `30d0bed2` and says the dogfood battery is not owed. The reviewed head is two commits later and declares the narrowing arm. The PR body reports the battery at this head, and `Dogfood Regression Gate` is success on it.
- One item is with the security seat.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts` (hits). The row holds. `@objectstack/plugin-hono-server` is the third emitter after `@objectstack/rest` and `@objectstack/service-storage`. The ledger's own status table already maps `PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE` to 413. The condition is the same on all three: the request carries more than the door accepts. The first consumer is `body-limit.ts`, which stamps the code on `RequestBodyTooLarge` and on the envelope.
- Nit N2: the row's comment says `createHonoApp` "imports the constant". It imports `RequestBodyTooLarge` and `requestBodyTooLargeAnswer`. `PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE_CODE` is not exported from the package index.

Ruling arms, in the code:
- 413 before reading, on a declared length, both doors: holds. `guardRequest` sets `declaredOverLimit`, and the guarded stream refuses on its first pull without opening the original body. `readRequestBody` (self-hosted) and `readDispatchBody` (`createHonoApp`) return the refusal before any read. A request forwarded whole to the auth service or a domain reads the guarded stream, and `installRequestBodyLimit` replaces the answer with 413 once the guard has refused a read.
- Counting on an undeclared length: holds. The guarded stream counts every chunk and refuses once the count passes the limit, also when a length was declared. The self-hosted pre-read of an undeclared JSON or form body goes through `hold()`, which stops after the chunk that passes the limit.
- Operator option: holds. The option wins, then `OS_HTTP_MAX_BODY_BYTES`, then 10 MiB. Zero, negative, fractional, non-finite and non-digit values throw where they are configured. The limit is read per request, so the setter applies to later requests.
- Upload doors keep their own bound: holds, as in ① above. Storage is not a dispatcher domain, so `createHonoApp` has no byte door to cap.
- The 413 envelope is the declared shape with a registered code, so the `{}` entry for `body-limit.ts` in `scripts/check-route-envelope.mjs` is right.

Findings:
- Should-fix S1: the code no longer agrees with the published `IHttpRequest` text in `packages/spec/src/contracts/http-server.ts`, a file outside this diff. That text says the standard transport answers a refused `body` read with 400 `INVALID_REQUEST`, that a handler must not catch the refusal and carry on, and that a handler needing raw bytes never reads `body`. At this head the transport also answers 413 `PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE`, and `uploadLinkFormBody` catches that refusal and reads `rawBody()`, after which `adapter.ts` drops the refusal. The take-over rule is stated only in `adapter.ts` jsdoc. The fix is contract text. It fits the next PR already ordered for the `rawBody` contract, if that PR's surface names it.
- Should-fix S2: `rawBody()` in `adapter.ts` is no longer repeatable for a body the transport did not pre-read. The first call consumes the original body. A second call falls through to `c.req.arrayBuffer()` on the guarded stream, which reads an already consumed body, where `main` served Hono's cached bytes. No caller in the tree reads twice. Keeping the first promise restores it.
- Nit N3: `HonoHttpServer` resolves `OS_HTTP_MAX_BODY_BYTES` in a field initialiser, before the plugin applies its option. A malformed variable therefore fails construction even when a valid `maxRequestBodyBytes` is given.
- Nit N4: the upload link's form is parsed two ways by size. Within the transport limit, Hono keeps the last value of a repeated name. Over it, `uploadLinkFormBody` keeps a list, which the form checks refuse. A well-formed form names each part once and is read the same on both paths.
- Nit N5: `body-limit.ts` and the changeset say a route that never reads the body reads nothing. That is true of the guard. The self-hosted door still pre-reads a JSON or form body, up to the limit, before the route runs, as on `main`.

S1 and S2 each earn a delta review of their fix. Neither breaks a ruling arm.

security#2 · os-tesla · session_01L9qibwMmGJKaQ52CgHqNu2

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `bb70828123790b3d9fdc3f58bdc1f8bf19389c2b`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/src/body-limit.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/src/request-body.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/src/adapter.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/src/hono-plugin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/src/index.ts, packages/adapters/hono/src/index.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/storage-routes.ts, scripts/check-route-envelope.mjs

Delta review of one commit on top of `e85a5062`, where record 6869167954 gave PASS with should-fix S1 and S2. The verdict covers the whole PR. Read this round: the delta `e85a5062..bb708281` (5 files), the updated PR body, and the check-runs on this head. Code the delta does not touch stands on the earlier reading. The rest of the diff (the test files and the changeset as prose) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

Check-runs on this head, all completed: 58 success, 13 skipped, 0 failed, 0 pending. `Check Changeset`, `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Spec property liveness`, `Type Check · workspace`, `Test Core` 1/8 to 8/8 and `Dogfood Regression Gate` are success.

### ① Derived judgments

- The accept sets and the public surface are as judged at `e85a5062`. The delta narrows and widens nothing a client or operator sees.
- `rawBody()` on the self-hosted door answers the same bytes on every call: right, and it restores what `main` did.
- `RequestBodyGuard` gains `release()`. The type is exported from the package index, so the published type surface grows by one method. `installRequestBodyLimit` is the only caller.
- The ledger row changes in its comment only. The code set and the row are unchanged.

### ② Semver level

- Unchanged and right: `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, `patch`, the `!` title, the BREAKING banner and one adr-0087 marker. The lines are identical in the PR body and the changeset.
- N1 is closed: the changeset frontmatter now lists `@objectstack/spec` at `patch`. That is the only changeset change. `Check Changeset` is success on this head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- S1 has moved to the next-PR remainder, and the PR body says so: under "Upload doors", the `rawBody` contract PR "updates the `IHttpRequest` contract's description of body refusals to include the 413". Accepted as the disposition of S1.
- Nit N6: that sentence names the 413 only. The same contract text also says a handler must not catch the refusal and carry on, and that a raw-bytes handler never reads `body`. The take-over in `uploadLinkFormBody` departs from both. The next PR's surface should name them as well.
- The dev's reason for not cancelling at the refusal itself is right in the code: `readAll()` continues from the same reader that `hold()` opened, so the byte-door and upload-link paths need it open.
- One item is with the security seat.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts` (hits). N2 is closed: the comment now names `RequestBodyTooLarge` and `requestBodyTooLargeAnswer`, which is what `createHonoApp` imports. The row holds as before.

`adapter.ts`, S2 closed. `rawBody()` keeps the first read's promise and returns it on every call. The size refusal is still cleared synchronously on each call. Pins: two cases in `body-limit.test.ts` call it twice and compare the bytes. The declared case is the path S2 named (a body the transport did not pre-read). The undeclared case is the held path.

`body-limit.ts`, the new `release()` arm. It holds.
- When it cancels: only when a held body passed the limit, the held reader is still open, and nothing claimed the rest. A body that fit, or one that ended, is never cancelled.
- A claimed reader is not cancelled. `readAll()` clears the open mark as its first statement, before any read. `rawBody()` reaches `readAll()` through a callback queued on the already settled hold. `release()` starts only after `next()` resolves and then waits on that same hold, so its check always runs after the callback. The mark is set before `release()` reads it.
- A read still in progress is not cancelled: the mark was cleared when that read began.
- Streaming responses: the adapter resolves the route only after the handler's promise settles, for a streamed answer too. So `release()` runs after the handler has finished, not while it runs.
- The guarded-stream path and `createHonoApp` do not use `hold()`, so `release()` is a no-op there.
- Pins: two cases (JSON and form, no declared length, an endless source) assert 413, the source cancelled, and at most the limit plus two chunks pulled. The PR body reports both red with the release removed.
- Nit N7: a handler that makes its first `rawBody()` call after its own promise has settled is past `release()`. `readAll()` then finds the reader closed and answers the bytes held so far as if they were the whole body. No route in the tree reads that late. Refusing in `readAll()` once released would make it explicit.
- Nit N8: no pin asserts directly that a claimed source is left uncancelled. The take-over and upload-link cases cover the bytes arriving whole.

Open from the earlier record, unchanged by the delta: nits N3, N4 and N5. Each is an accepted deviation or a follow-up.

No must-fix and no should-fix is open on this head.

**VERDICT: PASS**

**ACCEPT · 2026-11-14T02:30Z · PR #33172 · head `bb708281`**

1. **Shape:** `Refs #32004` (no public card), base `main`, 13 files (+1400/−19): the request-body guard and its wiring in `@objectstack/plugin-hono-server` and `@objectstack/hono`, the upload-link door's form bound in `@objectstack/service-storage`, one provenance row in the `packages/spec` error-code ledger, a route-envelope gate line, tests and a dogfood file, and one changeset (patch on four packages, `!`). `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, matching claim 6866240706 as amended by 6866365896, 6867307355 and 6869174593. Assignee `os-tesla`. Author `objectstack-fleet[bot]`.
2. **Premise:** the maintainer's choice of 2026-11-13 22:12Z in the seat thread. Both HTTP server doors refuse a request body over one limit with `413 PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE` before reading it. The limit is 10 MiB by default and operator-configurable, and upload doors keep their own larger bound.
3. **Contract review:** owed at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` (a `packages/spec` ledger row). Round 1 PASS 6869167954 carried two should-fix items. The delta review PASS 6870224380 on this head closes both and covers the whole PR. Its nits are accepted deviations or ride the named next PR: the `rawBody` bound as a contract change, which also updates the `IHttpRequest` refusal text.
4. **Prose faces, read sentence by sentence:** the changeset's BREAKING banner says who moves (an operator whose clients send JSON or form bodies over 10 MiB) and how to raise the limit, and that storage uploads are unchanged. The PR body states the rule and names its remainders: the `rawBody` contract bound, an unset `max_upload_mb`, and the docs follow-up for the two 413 cause lists.
5. **Gates / check-runs:** dev: 116 derived gates, 115 run, 1 NOT MEASURED (the teardown self-test, which needs a full clone; CI ran it), every run exit 0; ablations red, then restored; dogfood battery green. On head `bb708281`: 71 runs, 58 success, 13 skipped, 0 failed, 0 running; mergeable_state clean. `check-governed-merges --pr 33172`: NOT governed.
6. **Landing:** not governed, 1419 changed lines, K = 4 (PRBASE `88355328`, no new locale pack). The seat readies the PR and arms auto-merge under the maintainer's standing word 「车道经理应该使用 pm-dispatch 技能审核和落地pr」 (2026-11-13).
